page: OVHcloud rtx5000-84 is a GPU-accelerated server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon W-3235 processor with 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 threads running at 3.3 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 84.0 GB of system memory, providing 5.25 GB per core. For acceleration, the server is equipped with three NVIDIA Quadro RTX 5000 GPUs based on the Turing architecture, delivering a combined 48 GB of VRAM. Local storage consists of a 400 GB SSD, and network connectivity is supported by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data highlights strong performance in memory and parallel processing tasks. The system achieves a Passmark memory score of 2913.07, placing it in the top 25% tier. Large-block memory write bandwidth is a relative bottleneck at 25.38 GB/sec, and single-threaded gzip compression is also in the lower quartile at 23.78 GB/sec. However, the multi-GPU setup excels in parallelized workloads, particularly LLM inference. Prompt processing speeds reach top-tier levels, achieving 8884.89 tokens/sec for a 135M model, 1827.36 tokens/sec for a 7B model, and 220.48 tokens/sec for a 70B model. Text generation speeds are also highly competitive, with the 7B model generating 65.53 tokens/sec and the 70B model generating 7.46 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the rtx5000-84 offers a dense multi-GPU configuration on a dedicated single-socket host, making it a viable alternative to more expensive enterprise-grade accelerator instances. The inclusion of three physical GPUs with dedicated CPU cores provides balanced resource allocation without hyperthreading overhead. This server is highly suited for workloads such as large language model inference, parallelized data science jobs, 3D rendering, and machine learning workloads that benefit from multi-GPU scaling and high baseline network throughput.
